children: S&P Dow Jones Indices (S&P DJI) said on Friday it will change the eligibility criteria for S&P/TSX Canadian Indices, with the move potentially opening the door to the inclusion of major copper producer Anglo-Teck, according to investors.

Under the new criteria, foreign issuers listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange but neither domiciled nor incorporated in Canada could qualify for inclusion if they have a material and substantive connection to Canada. Previously, only TSX-listed companies domiciled or incorporated in Canada were eligible.
S&P/TSX Canadian Indices include the TSX Composite, Canada's benchmark stock index.
$53 billion all-stock merger with TSX Composite company Teck Resources
is expected to close ​between September and March, which would create the world's fifth-largest copper producer.
Under the proposed deal, the new company Anglo Teck will be headquartered in Canada but have a primary stock listing in London.

"It is highly likely that Anglo Tech will be permitted to remain in the S&P/TSX Composite Index under the proposed methodology," said Robert Gill, a portfolio manager at Fairbank Investment Management.
"Its attachment to Canada remains unusually strong — it brings a substantial Canadian economic footprint, with headquarters in Vancouver and plenty of spending in Canada for the foreseeable future."
The change comes after a consultation with market participants that was launched in July. Implementation is planned for December 21, 2026.
